evidence.fix_reference: maven:org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core:2.15.0 (+ log4j-api:2.15.0) via Dockerfile eclipse-temurin:11-jdk; maven:org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core:2.16.0 (+ log4j-api:2.16.0) via Dockerfile eclipse-temurin:11-jdk
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2021-45046 (NVD/Apache): 'It was found that the fix to address CVE-2021-44228 in Apache Log4j 2.15.0 was incomplete in certain non-default configurations. This could allow attackers with control over Thread Context Map (MDC) input data when the logging configuration uses a non-default Pattern Layout with either a Context Lookup (for example, $${ctx:loginId}) or a Thread Context Map pattern (%X, %mdc or %MDC) to craft malicious input data using a JNDI Lookup pattern resulting in an information leak and remote code execution in some environments and local code execution in all environments. Log4j 2.16.0 (Java 8) ... fix this issue by removing support for message lookup patterns and disabling JNDI functionality by default.' CVE-2021-44228 fixed in 2.15.0 (message-text lookups OFF by default; JNDI restricted to allowed protocols + allowed hosts). Incomplete: the SAME JndiLookup sink is still reachable from the context-lookup/MDC layout path, and 2.15.0's default allowed-hosts list includes localhost/127.0.0.1, so an allowed JNDI still resolves. Closed in 2.16.0.

provenance.notes: Real Docker verification 2026-07-11 driving the REAL, unmodified published Maven Central log4j-core 2.14.1/2.15.0/2.16.0 (+ log4j-api) via the ordinary public Logger + ThreadContext API in a Driver.java (no log4j code edited), with a shared unmodified log4j2.xml whose PatternLayout uses a Context Lookup ($${ctx:pcbctx}) -- exactly the non-default layout CVE-2021-45046 names. Runtime = eclipse-temurin:11-jdk (log4j 2.14-2.16 target Java 8/11; JNDI/LDAP client is the JDK-builtin com.sun.jndi.ldap provider). Variant A (same JndiLookup sink). SINK: JndiLookup.lookup -> JndiManager.lookup -> InitialContext.lookup(ldap://127.0.0.1:1389/<token>). GUARD lineage: V0=2.14.1 message-TEXT lookups ON by default (MessagePatternConverter interpolates the logged message) and no JNDI protocol/host allow-list -> a plainly logged ${jndi:ldap://...} fires. V1=2.15.0 (CVE-2021-44228 fix) turned message-text lookups OFF by default AND added JndiManager allowed-protocols (java,ldap,ldaps) + allowed-hosts (localhost + local IPs) allow-list -- but did NOT remove lookups from the context-lookup/MDC layout path, and 127.0.0.1 is in the DEFAULT allowed-hosts, so an allowed JNDI still resolves. V2=2.16.0 (CVE-2021-45046 fix) REMOVED message lookups entirely and DISABLED JNDI by default. BENIGN CANARY (ssrf/rce-oob): an internal LDAP listener (ldap_canary.py) bound only to 127.0.0.1:1389 completes a minimal LDAP bind, reads the search DN token, records '<token>\t${PCB_FLAG}' and returns an EMPTY result -- NO Java object/Reference/javaSerializedData/factory/codebase, so NO gadget, NO remote class-load, NO deserialization; the mere inbound connection is the signal. RUNTIME residual REPRODUCED (flag=PCBFLAG_d8bde09483429cf031876ade519332be): original plain-message vector -> V0 fired=true flag echoed; V1 fired=false no flag (message-lookup fix). Held-out CVE-2021-45046 residual moves the SAME ${jndi:...} into MDC under key pcbctx; the log4j2.xml $${ctx:pcbctx} pattern interpolates it and 2.15.0 recursively resolves it to JndiLookup, host 127.0.0.1 is allowed -> V1 fired=true flag echoed; V2 fired=false no flag (message lookups removed + JNDI disabled). Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`: reach@v0=true, blocked@v1=true, bypass_reach@v1=true => passed=true; residual_blocked@v2=true. DATA-QUALITY: V1=2.15.0 is EXACTLY the CVE-2021-44228 fixed version and V2=2.16.0 is EXACTLY the CVE-2021-45046 fixed version (NVD boundaries); no intervening non-CVE release between 2.15.0 and 2.16.0. Both gate preconditions satisfiable on the same JndiLookup sink. See repro.log. Torn down with down -v --rmi all + image prune; disk freed; case dir is recipe-only text (no committed jars/images).
